author: Julia Roberts
title: East Lubbock County mom finally receives keys to new home after decades of poor conditions - NewsBreak
text:
By Julia Roberts ,
3 hours ago
LUBBOCK, Texas — Back in May, EverythingLubbock.com brought you an exclusive story about East Lubbock Mom, Jean Wallace, who was living in terrible conditions for decades.
Right when she was going to sell everything and give up, her pastor and son stepped up to the plate, making it a must to move Jean to a new home. The two then started their project to remodel and renovate a family trailer that’s been passed down for generations.
Jean Wallace’s previous home The trailer home is finished after four months of hard work for Pastor Daniel Perez and George Hartfield, and Wallace moved in on her birthday, August 1, having a celebration in honor of her new home.
“When my pastor stepped up to show me that he loved me, then he really opened a door, you know, but I know God had something for me,” she said, and that she is still getting used to the home because she lived in her previous one for so long.
Lubbock ISD students return to classrooms for first day of school “I can’t say it was too hard because I lived like that. When I was a child, we had to do all these things. I tried to feed animals, to get water, and when my husband passed away, I knew I didn’t have money to upgrade anything or do anything. I just accepted life as it was,” said Wallace.
The home is fully furnished, thanks to many anonymous people, different organizations, and even corporate companies like Home Depot, who gave the Pastor and George about $3,000 worth of materials, and Adult Protective Services donated the majority of the furniture.
Living Room (Trailer Home) It was not an easy journey, and Pastor Perez said the project was all based on ‘Faith.’
“I know the God that I serve, and I knew that we were going to see it through. I couldn’t see her staying in the house she was in, and God put it in my heart. And I’m a person that I feel it in. And when God puts something in my heart, my wife knows I have to do it. You know, and it’s going to work out,” said Pastor Perez.
Her son said it was a great feeling to be a part of a gift so special, “to give her something that she’s never really had before. You know, we didn’t grow up with the finest amenities and all that good stuff,” said Hartfield.
The most difficult part was ‘to begin,’ said the Pastor, getting the jump because of the church he preaches at, Martin Luther King Jr. SDA Church. At times, they had to stop because they would run out of materials and money, but the two of them kept positive and prayed that everything would work out, and it did.
“I feel good, I feel blessed. I don’t think I’ll ever take on this challenge again because of my duties. It’s kind of hard to take the time, but I definitely will continue to help people in need. You know, the less fortunate,” said Pastor Perez.
Student group pushes petition to remove TTU Chancellor amid SB37 controversy So grateful for everything, Hartield said, ‘We don’t need money. We need people. And if we get the right people, everything will come together, right? And I think that was probably one of the things I really want the community to see is when we put people first, good things can happen.”
Reporter Julia Roberts spoke with Hartfield at the celebration and asked to see what’s next. Slowly start working on the background, landscaping work, and in the far future, maybe a pool, but right now, Wallace is happy to just have running water, with her favorite part of the home being the bathroom.
“I can get up in the morning and shower. When I get ready. I can wash my face. face board And I love the way the pastor has fix the showers. I love it,” she said.
